description: Examine major cognitive and psychometric theories of human intelligence, analyzing Spearman's g factor, Gardner's multiple intelligences, Sternberg's triarchic model, and emotional intelligence.

slides.title: The Nature of Human Intellect
slides.content:
# The Architecture of Human Intelligence

What is **intelligence**? David Wechsler defined it as:
> *"The aggregate or global capacity of the individual to act purposefully, to think rationally, and to deal effectively with their environment."*

For over a century, psychologists debated: Is intelligence a **single, unitary general ability**, or is it a collection of **multiple, independent cognitive talents**?

```
                             [THE THEORETICAL LANDSCAPE OF INTELLECT]
                                                |
         +--------------------------------------+--------------------------------------+
         |                                                                             |
   [UNITARY PSYCHOMETRIC MODELS]                                 [MULTIDIMENSIONAL & SYSTEMS MODELS]
   - Spearman's General Factor (g)                               - Gardner's Multiple Intelligences (8 Intelligences)
   - Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) Gf-Gc Theory                     - Sternberg's Triarchic Theory (Analytical, Creative, Practical)
   - Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory (P-FIT)                  - Emotional Intelligence (Salovey, Mayer, & Goleman)
```

slides.title: Charles Spearman's General Factor: The 'g' Factor (1904)
slides.content:
# Charles Spearman: The Discovery of 'g'

In 1904, English psychologist Charles Spearman examined children's academic test scores across vastly different subjects (Latin, Math, Geometry, Pitch Discrimination).

## The Positive Manifold:
Spearman discovered a universal mathematical reality: **People who score high on one cognitive test tend to score high on all other cognitive tests**, regardless of subject matter!

```
                                    [GENERAL INTELLIGENCE (g)]
                                                 |
         +-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+-------------------+
         |                   |                   |                   |                   |
     [Spatial (s1)]     [Verbal (s2)]     [Math (s3)]         [Memory (s4)]       [Logic (s5)]
```

## Spearman's Two-Factor Theory:
- **g Factor (General Intelligence):** A shared, global biological mental energy underlying all cognitive operations.
- **s Factors (Specific Abilities):** Unique skills specific to a particular task (e.g., musical pitch sensitivity).

slides.title: Cattell & Horn: Fluid vs. Crystallized Intelligence
slides.content:
# Raymond Cattell & John Horn: Gf vs. Gc

In 1963, Raymond Cattell deconstructed Spearman's general factor into two distinct, fundamentally different types of intelligence:

```
   FLUID INTELLIGENCE (Gf)                       CRYSTALLIZED INTELLIGENCE (Gc)
   +---------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------+
   | - Raw, biological, innate capacity.   |     | - Accumulated factual knowledge,       |
   | - Abstract reasoning, pattern solving,|       vocabulary, skills, and cultural wisdom.|
   |   rapid working memory processing.    |     | - Acquired through formal schooling    |
   | - Independent of culture or schooling.|       and life experience.                   |
   | - PEAKS IN EARLY 20s, THEN DECLINES!  |     | - STEADILY INCREASES ACROSS LIFESPAN!  |
   +---------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------+
```

An 80-year-old professor has declining Fluid Intelligence (solving novel spatial puzzles slower), but peak Crystallized Intelligence (vast vocabulary, deep semantic knowledge)!

slides.content: Verify your understanding of Spearman's g and Cattell's Gf-Gc model!
slides.quizQuestion: According to Raymond Cattell and John Horn, how does 'Crystallized Intelligence' (Gc) typically change across the healthy adult lifespan compared to 'Fluid Intelligence' (Gf)?
quizOptions: Crystallized intelligence peaks at age 18 and collapses by age 30

Crystallized intelligence is found only in newborn infants

slides.title: The Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) Model
slides.content:
# The Pinnacle of Psychometrics: The CHC Model

Today, the most empirically validated psychometric framework in cognitive science is the **Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) Theory** (McGrew, 2005):

```
   [STRATUM III: GENERAL ABILITY (g)]  --> The apex: General cognitive power.
                  ^
                  |
   [STRATUM II: BROAD COGNITIVE ABILITIES (~10 Broad Domains)]
   - Fluid Reasoning (Gf)                - Processing Speed (Gs)
   - Crystallized Knowledge (Gc)         - Short-Term Working Memory (Gsm)
   - Visual-Spatial Processing (Gv)      - Long-Term Retrieval (Glr)
   - Auditory Processing (Ga)            - Quantitative Knowledge (Gq)
                  ^
                  |
   [STRATUM I: NARROW COGNITIVE ABILITIES (~70+ Highly Specific Skills)]
   - Word reading speed, phonetic coding, memory span, associative memory, visualization.
```

Modern tests like the WAIS-IV and Woodcock-Johnson-IV are structured directly upon CHC theory.

slides.title: Howard Gardner's Theory of Multiple Intelligences (1983)
slides.content:
# Howard Gardner: Frames of Mind

Harvard psychologist **Howard Gardner** rejected traditional IQ tests as narrow linguistic-mathematical gatekeepers, proposing **Multiple Intelligences (MI)**:

```
   1. LINGUISTIC:            Mastery of language, rhetoric, poetry, writing (Shakespeare).
   2. LOGICAL-MATHEMATICAL:  Abstract logical reasoning, mathematics, scientific analysis (Einstein).
   3. SPATIAL:               Mental visualization, architectural manipulation (Michelangelo).
   4. MUSICAL:               Rhythmic pitch, tone, compositional sensitivity (Mozart).
   5. BODILY-KINESTHETIC:    Motor control, athletic dexterity, surgical finesse (Simone Biles).
   6. INTERPERSONAL:         Empathy, social leadership, understanding others (Martin Luther King Jr.).
   7. INTRAPERSONAL:         Self-awareness, emotional self-regulation, deep self-knowledge.
   8. NATURALISTIC:          Recognizing and classifying ecological flora and fauna (Charles Darwin).
```

*Scientific Critique:* Cognitive psychometricians note that Gardner's intelligences correlate with each other, reflecting underlying g, and represent "talents" rather than distinct autonomous intelligences.

slides.title: Robert Sternberg's Triarchic Theory of Intelligence
slides.content:
# Robert Sternberg: Successful Intelligence (1985)

Robert Sternberg argued that intelligence is the ability to achieve personal success in life within one's sociocultural context through the balance of three faculties: **The Triarchic Theory**:

```
                                  [TRIARCHIC INTELLIGENCE]
                                             |
         +-----------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
         |                                   |                                   |
   [ANALYTICAL INTELLIGENCE]           [CREATIVE INTELLIGENCE]             [PRACTICAL INTELLIGENCE]
   - Componential processing.          - Experiential processing.          - Contextual adaptation.
   - Academic problem-solving,         - Generating novel solutions;       - "Street smarts"; tacit knowledge;
     analyzing, evaluating, testing.     adapting to unique challenges.      shaping and selecting environments.
   - Measured by standard IQ tests.    - Synthetic insight and invention.  - Managing everyday life demands.
```

High academic Analytical IQ guarantees nothing in career success without Practical tacit knowledge!

slides.title: Emotional Intelligence (EI / EQ): Goleman & Salovey
slides.content:
# The Emotional Mind: Emotional Intelligence

Peter Salovey and John Mayer (1990) defined **Emotional Intelligence (EI)**, popularized globally by Daniel Goleman (1995):

## The Mayer-Salovey-Caruso Four-Branch Ability Model (MSCEIT):

```
   [BRANCH 4: MANAGING EMOTIONS]   --> Regulating emotions in oneself and others (calming anger).
                 ^
                 |
   [BRANCH 3: UNDERSTANDING EMOTIONS]--> Analyzing emotional blends and transitions (grief -> anger).
                 ^
                 |
   [BRANCH 2: USING EMOTIONS]      --> Harnessing emotions to facilitate creative thinking and focus.
                 ^
                 |
   [BRANCH 1: PERCEIVING EMOTIONS] --> Accurately reading facial micro-expressions and body language.
```

High EI predicts superior leadership, marital longevity, and lower clinical burnout in healthcare professionals.

slides.title: Creativity & Intelligence: Divergent Thinking
slides.content:
# Thinking Outside the Box: Creativity

What is the relationship between intelligence and creativity? J.P. Guilford distinguished between two cognitive pathways:

```
   CONVERGENT THINKING (Traditional IQ)          DIVERGENT THINKING (Creativity)
   +---------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------+
   - Zeroes in on the SINGLE correct answer|     - Radiates outward in multiple directions|
     to a structured problem.              |       generating NOVEL, UNORTHODOX solutions.|
   - Standard multiple-choice math exams.  |     - Measured via Torrance Tests (TTCT).    |
   +---------------------------------------+     +----------------------------------------+
```

## The Threshold Hypothesis of Creativity:
Above an IQ of approx 120, the correlation between IQ and creative achievement weakens significantly: high intelligence is necessary, but **not sufficient on its own** to guarantee creative genius.

slides.title: The Neurobiology of Intelligence: P-FIT Theory
slides.content:
# Where Does Intelligence Live? P-FIT Theory

Rex Jung and Richard Haier (2007) synthesized neuroimaging data into the **Parieto-Frontal Integration Theory (P-FIT)** of human intelligence:

```
   Step 1: Temporal & Occipital Lobes  --> Sensory encoding of visual and auditory stimuli.
                     |
                     v
   Step 2: Parietal Cortex (Angular)    --> Structural abstraction and spatial-symbolic integration.
                     |
                     v
   Step 3: Prefrontal Cortex (dlPFC)   --> Hypothesis testing, working memory, and decision evaluation.
                     |
                     v
   Step 4: Anterior Cingulate (ACC)    --> Action selection and inhibition of incorrect responses.
```

## The Neural Efficiency Hypothesis:
Brighter brains are not working harder; fMRI and PET scans show that high-IQ individuals exhibit **LOWER glucose metabolism and greater neural efficiency** when solving complex problems!

slides.title: EI & Neuroscience of Intellect Check
slides.content: Verify your understanding of emotional intelligence and brain networks!
slides.quizQuestion: According to the Neural Efficiency Hypothesis of intelligence (Haier et al.), what do functional brain scans (fMRI/PET) reveal when high-IQ individuals solve moderately complex cognitive tasks?
quizOptions: Their brains consume ten times more glucose and overheat
Their brains exhibit greater neural efficiency, consuming LESS glucose and activating focused, streamlined neural networks compared to lower-IQ peers
Their temporal lobes shut down completely
Their brains show identical activation to sleeping subjects

slides.title: Cross-Cultural Definitions of Intelligence
slides.content:
# What Does it Mean to Be Smart Across Cultures?

Western psychology defines intelligence primarily as **individual cognitive processing speed, abstract analysis, and linguistic sharpness**:

```
   WESTERN DEFINITIONS                           NON-WESTERN / COLLECTIVIST DEFINITIONS
   ----------------------------------------      -------------------------------------------
   - Rapid problem solving ("Quick thinker").    - Deliberate, contemplative reflection.
   - Abstract logic isolated from context.       - Social responsibility and interpersonal warmth.
   - Technological problem mastery.              - Practical moral wisdom and respect for elders.
```

- **Rural Africa (Serpell, 1993):** The Chewa concept of *nzelu* includes both intellectual cleverness (*chenjela*) and social/moral responsibility (*tumikila*). A clever person who is arrogant or unhelpful is considered unintelligent!

slides.title: Artificial General Intelligence vs. Human Wisdom
slides.content:
# The Silicon Challenge: AI vs. Human Mind

As Large Language Models and AI systems match humans on standardized exams, cognitive scientists highlight fundamental differences:

## Moravec's Paradox (Hans Moravec, 1988):
*"It is comparatively easy to make computers exhibit adult level performance on intelligence tests or playing checkers, and difficult or impossible to give them the skills of a one-year-old when it comes to perception and mobility."*

Computers execute fast statistical pattern calculations; humans possess **Embodied Cognition, Phenomenological Consciousness, and Existential Purpose**.

slides.title: Practical Applications in Education and Leadership
slides.content:
# Applying Intelligence Frameworks

- **Differentiated Instruction:** Designing classroom curricula that engage analytical, creative, and practical cognitive pathways (Sternberg).
- **Leadership Development:** Hiring executives based not merely on raw GMA, but on high emotional intelligence and social self-regulation (Goleman).
- **Lifelong Cognitive Health:** Leveraging crystallized knowledge and intellectual curiosity to build **Cognitive Reserve**, buffering against neurodegenerative dementia.

quizOptions: It requires memorizing mathematical formulas in under 10 seconds

slides.title: Theoretical Models Comparison Matrix
slides.content:
# Theoretical Architecture of Intelligence Models

| Model | Core Construct | Structural Typology | Key Pioneer |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Two-Factor Model** | General mental energy (g) | Single apex + specific s factors | Charles Spearman (1904) |
| **Primary Mental Abilities**| 7 independent mental faculties | Multi-factor without apex | Louis Thurstone (1938) |
| **Gf-Gc Theory** | Fluid vs Crystallized Intellect | Biological raw vs Acquired cultural | Raymond Cattell (1963) |
| **CHC Model** | 3 Strata: General, Broad, Narrow | Hierarchical taxonomic consensus | Cattell-Horn-Carroll |
| **Multiple Intelligences** | 8 semi-autonomous intelligences | Modular brain-based talents | Howard Gardner (1983) |
| **Triarchic Theory** | Analytical, Creative, Practical | Information processing & context | Robert Sternberg (1985) |
| **Emotional Intelligence**| 4 branches of emotional ability | Emotion-cognition integration | Salovey & Mayer (1990) |

slides.title: The Ongoing Synthesis of Human Intellect
slides.content:
# The Modern Synthesis of Intelligence

Modern cognitive neuroscience bridges psychometrics and systems models:

- Spearman's **g** reflects biological neural efficiency, white matter tract integrity, and prefrontal working memory volume (P-FIT).
- Yet human real-world success requires Sternberg's **Practical Wisdom**, Gardner's **Diverse Talents**, and Goleman's **Emotional Compassion**.

slides.title: Module Synthesis: Theories of Intelligence
slides.content:
# Key Takeaways: Theories of Intelligence

```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                 MODULE SUMMARY MATRIX                                   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Concept / Model       | Key Pioneers                | Core Scientific Principle         |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| General Factor (g)    | Charles Spearman (1904)     | Positive manifold: All cognitive  |
|                       |                             | tests correlate via shared g.     |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Fluid vs Crystallized | Raymond Cattell (1963)      | Gf (raw reasoning) peaks early;   |
|                       |                             | Gc (accumulated wisdom) grows.    |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Triarchic Theory      | Robert Sternberg (1985)     | Analytical, Creative, and         |
|                       |                             | Practical Successful Intellect.   |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
| Neural Efficiency     | Richard Haier (2007)        | P-FIT: High-IQ brains process with|
| Hypothesis            |                             | streamlined lower glucose drain.  |
+-----------------------+-----------------------------+-----------------------------------+
```

## Final Lesson:
Human intellect is not a single number on a scorecard; it is a dynamic, multidimensional symphony of neural efficiency, creative divergence, and cultural wisdom that adapts humanity to an ever-evolving world.
